findings.title: Genuine parser edges made publication artifacts unavailable.
findings.reproduction: Construct a draft/index using parseRepositoryIndex with a real exported TypeScript function, then call buildPublicationArtifact. The original spread retained local extraction metadata rejected by strict published GraphEdge validation.
findings.observedBeforeFix: Invalid published edge shape; focused suite failed during setup with zero cases executed.
findings.fixObserved: Published edges explicitly project the shared GraphEdge contract before signing.
findings.regression: exports only the selected real files and graph, with genuine publisher signatures

findings.title: Authenticated commerce reads attempted row locks without UPDATE privilege.
findings.reproduction: Use AtlasDatabase with the actual migrations and authenticated role to call createPurchase or history. member() originally executed FOR SHARE in a principal transaction.
findings.observedBeforeFix: AtlasDatabaseError code=permission; 22 of 24 buyer cases failed before usable quoting/history.
findings.fixObserved: Principal read transactions use nonlocking membership reads; trusted mutation transactions retain row locks without granting authenticated UPDATE.
findings.regression: atomically reserves approved integer units from a configured allowance with a genuine offline SDK quote

findings.title: Provider ledger reauthorization required a nested database connection.
findings.reproduction: Run an authorized offline provider request through the genuine runtime/ledger while the fixture pool rejects acquisition of another connection from inside its existing transaction.
findings.observedBeforeFix: HTTP 503 instead of the expected unpaid HTTP 402; currentArtifact opened a second transaction during ledger lookup/quote reauthorization.
findings.fixObserved: Ledger fresh checks carry the existing AtlasTransaction; currentArtifact uses it instead of acquiring another pool connection.
findings.regression: issues an authorized offline quote without acquiring a second pool connection inside a ledger transaction
findings.limitation: This reproduces connection reentrancy, not multi-connection PostgreSQL contention.

importHistoryCapacity.scope: Independent regression of retained import history through actual AtlasDatabase transactions, SQL triggers, authorization queries, parser evidence and repository service methods. No production or shared implementation edits.

method.database: Isolated PGlite PostgreSQL-WASM database; generated UUID workspaces and bounded generate_series fixtures of at most 100 snapshots / 1000 jobs each.
method.source: Two small generated package/TypeScript files, real parseRepositoryIndex output, actual source_files/graphs rows and immutable synthetic Git identity. Imported source is parsed, never executed.
method.injectedBoundary: Server-owned GitHub principal adapter returns synthetic Clerk/GitHub authority and exact commit/tree proof. No network, live credentials, external source or paid calls.
method.concurrencyLimit: The fixture serializes AtlasDatabase connections onto one PGlite backend. It executes advisory locks and SQL constraints but does not establish contention safety across separate PostgreSQL backends.

finalChecks.command: bunx tsc --noEmit --module ESNext --moduleResolution Bundler --target ES2022 --lib ES2023,DOM --skipLibCheck --strict --noUncheckedIndexedAccess --exactOptionalPropertyTypes --allowImportingTsExtensions --types node tests/integration/import-history-capacity.test.ts

verifiedChecks: Actual 001 SQL admits retained snapshot 100 and rejects 101 with P0001 / Workspace retained snapshot capacity reached, including failed and cancelled versions in the total; stored source remains unchanged.
Actual 001 SQL admits retained job 1000 and rejects 1001 with P0001 / Workspace retained import job capacity reached, including complete, failed and cancelled history in the total.

assertImportHistoryCapacity acquires pg_advisory_xact_lock for atlas-import-capacity:<workspace UUID>. At 100 snapshots / 999 jobs it permits another job for an existing snapshot and rejects a new snapshot. At 99 snapshots / 1000 jobs it rejects either kind of new import work.
Capacity rejection has RepositoryServiceError code import-history-limit, HTTP 422 and the exact actionable message asking an administrator to review retention before importing another version.

While the first workspace retains 100 snapshots / 1000 jobs, another workspace's actual queueImport accepts one snapshot and one job. Its member cannot read the first workspace's retained source index.

At both limits, two actual queueImport calls for the completed exact commit reuse its existing snapshot and return jobId null without acquiring a capacity lock or adding rows. getIndex preserves all parser nodes/evidence/files; getGraph search returns the retained symbol; getSource returns the original exact line range; the persisted source and graph are unchanged.

At both limits, actual queueImport reuses the same existing queued job and the same existing running job. Authenticated getJob remains readable, and the older completed source remains readable without deletion.

New-version queueImport is rejected at 100 snapshots / 999 jobs and at 99 snapshots / 1000 jobs. The transaction rolls back prior repository visibility/installation metadata writes, leaves no partial new snapshot and preserves all source.
